analysis: CHANGELOG.md only: the base units (lines 3015-3443) are older release history, and the head unit is the new v0.10.6 candidate section (lines 11-135 visible). The PR changes no executable code, so no security control is directly altered. The text does describe security-relevant behavior that the next pass should check against code and platform sources it does not include: (1) two-Mac cluster pairing and registration via `cluster_runtime`, with approvals derived from releases and the `EIGENINFERENCE_CLUSTER_PAIR_*` coordinator settings (TB-002, TB-011, A-015/A-016/A-017). (2) The `darkbloom cluster local` API, which binds to every network on the leading Mac unless `--bind` is given and uses the same key as `start --local`. This is a deliberate, documented exposure that may need a threat-model entry. (3) An owner-only `provider.toml` and `umask 022` extraction in the updater (TB-003). (4) Control-leader claims, lease and failover over the pairing-keyed link. (5) Per-cluster SSD prefix records (T-041), documented as bound to the artifact, both builds and the MTP policy, with `balanced` quantized records and a prefix agreement field change. These records keep the HMAC names, the KEK and the TTL unchanged per the entry. No evidence in the supplied text contradicts T-041's posture, but the cluster tier's cache scoping and sharing across accounts is not visible here. (6) Error-code changes (400 for unknown content parts, 422 for truncated `response_format`) are client-visible only. The changelog is a claim, not proof, so the actual cluster, link-authentication and approval code is outside this evidence. Flag for deeper review of the cluster trust boundary, which has no TB entry in the supplied threat model.
